# Meanwhile — Sean's standing decisions

Adopted as a consolidated replacement — September 25, 2026. Adoption records Sean's approval of this wording; it does not prove approval of older AI-written rulings.

## 1. Sean sets the direction; agents own delivery

Sean sets the goals, priorities, business policies, and spending authority. Agents make the engineering decisions needed to complete the work. Sean's current explicit instructions take priority over older project instructions.

**Stay on the original objective until it is completed, a fatal error derails it, or Sean changes it.** A routine failure, difficult source, slow test, or unfinished dependency is not a fatal error. If a fatal error makes the objective impossible under current conditions, show the evidence, preserve the work, and identify recovery options. Do not quietly substitute another objective. Honor explicit pauses and continue independent work.

Plan backward from the full requested result. Identify essential dependencies before building. Required connections must work and be verified before the assignment is finished. A handoff, passing component test, or working screen does not prove the whole system works. Building a car that backs out of the driveway does not satisfy a request for a car that gets to the grocery store.

Meanwhile must acquire and present information across expanding geographic coverage. Admin must support adding and tracking ZIPs, counties, metros, and states through work creation, discovery, acquisition, verification, and public delivery. Test expansion beyond existing pilot coverage. Necessary connections are part of the assignment, not optional future work.

**Build general capabilities without preparing a specific test ZIP.** Do not perform target-specific scouting, source mapping, manual data filling, or special-case repairs in advance of an expansion test. General fixes must work through the normal system. Preserve and disclose preparation already performed; do not erase accumulated knowledge or describe a prepared scope as an untouched test. Fix material blockers, preserve required verification and release gates, and reuse valid evidence rather than expanding the assignment with minor improvements, broad rechecks, or unchanged repeated attempts. (Sean, September 26, 2026, in the release-usage accounting instruction.)

## 2. Get the public information to readers

**Find a way to get the information, parse it, verify it, and push it to readers.** Finding a link or knowing information exists is not completion. A failed route does not end the obligation.

Think like the world's greatest detective: What are we missing? How else could we get it? What have we not tried? Follow promising clues, combine sources, and build missing tools or acquisition methods. A checklist or fixed number of attempts is not the limit. Creating a route means obtaining real evidence, never inventing facts.

Investigate what already worked. Trace existing data and working reader links through their sources, tools, stored evidence, code, and history. Establish what changed; reuse, repair, or learn from the earlier method. Past success is evidence to investigate, not a guarantee that the same route still works.

During discovery and ongoing coverage, search broadly for current information about each body being worked and compare it with what Meanwhile shows. Do this even when connected feeds work. Follow search results to underlying evidence, confirm the body and current details, and recover missing information. A healthy feed does not prove complete coverage. Sean must not be the system's search engine or quality control.

Use relevant resources Sean has provided. Check the current tool inventory and learned methods, including government APIs, feeds, search services, browser navigation, and document links. Legistar, Census, LegiScan, Brave, and Exa are examples, not an exhaustive list. Use search early when useful; do not force every free option ahead of a better paid tool within the agreed budget. Confirm that the integration actually exposes and uses the needed capability. Avoid irrelevant calls and reuse valid evidence.

Before escalating a retrieval blocker, challenge it with another appropriate method and evidence of prior success. Record the actual routes, results, missing information, and next approach. Distinguish discovery, access, extraction, verification, publication, and display problems. One failed step does not establish that the information is unavailable. “Not found in the sources checked” must not become “does not exist.”

**Robots.txt alone does not block acquisition.** Automated reading of publicly accessible pages is authorized even when robots.txt asks otherwise. Record what robots.txt says as evidence, but do not stop reading, remove coverage, or ask Sean again about individual publishers or groups solely because of it. This does not authorize bypassing authentication or other access controls. When retrieval technically fails, use alternative public routes and the available tools above; one failed route is not a completed investigation. Existing spending limits and the paid-research pause still apply. (Sean, September 25, 2026, in the Admin completion instructions. It replaces the per-publisher robots.txt questions prepared that day.)

## 3. Publish verified information promptly

**Information that passes verification publishes automatically.** No election-based delay or routine per-record approval. Publish as results become ready; do not wait for an entire hunt, state, or unrelated build. Keep unverified information out of publication and keep working to obtain and verify it.

Once the full hunt starts, we cannot go days without new information reaching readers. When delivery stalls, find and fix the failing step. Attempts, busy agents, stored files, and unchanged records do not count as newly delivered information. Deliver time-sensitive information while people can still use it.

Missing information must not hide independently verified information. Meeting schedules, publisher agenda links, and extracted agenda contents are separate capabilities. A missing agenda or location must not suppress an otherwise verified meeting. Preserve working links; distinguish “not yet published” from “not yet acquired.” Combine complementary sources with clear attribution and preserve verified dates, cancellations, and reschedules when changing routes.

Use officially published meeting addresses for map pins after normal source and location validation. Sean does not need to certify them personally. Keep source and reviewer attribution truthful; investigate ambiguity instead of inventing details. Give comparable people and sides a fair research effort.

## 4. Keep meeting coverage current

Maintain an active, rolling **90-day window of upcoming meetings**. Continue discovery after dates are posted: new meetings, changes, cancellations, and reschedules can appear at any time. Do not invent unpublished dates or delete history to maintain the window. Finding a meeting after it starts does not satisfy the goal of helping people attend.

Meeting discovery stays on. Sean controls paid search separately through Admin. Respect the current setting and spending limits; do not treat a paid-search pause as a pause on all discovery.

Check meeting sources:

- **Twice daily** generally.
- **Hourly, within 60 minutes**, for bodies with a meeting in the **next seven days OR concluded in the previous seven days**.

The seven-day window rolls automatically. Checks cover calendars, agendas, changes, cancellations, decisions, and minutes. This cadence is separate from the forward coverage window and does not change other data families' schedules.

Do not add an unapproved timing allowance. Verify that prioritizing one group does not repeatedly delay another beyond its required cadence. Claims that a delay happens only once need evidence; otherwise investigate and fix the recurring cause.

## 5. Build, test, verify, promote, and finish

**Waiting is not the plan. Work effectively and efficiently.** Start ready work immediately. Challenge long estimates across every active session before relaying them and whenever the plan changes. Include release queues, runner handoffs, scheduled cycles, and verification windows. Sean must not have to challenge each delay.

Keep a brief execution plan with each remaining task, one accountable owner, its actual dependency, justified duration, and earliest start. Base estimates on remaining work and measured check durations. Separate active work from idle time. Do not replace an unsupported long estimate with an unsupported shorter promise.

Run independent work in parallel without conflicting edits or interfering tests. Prepare downstream work as soon as its inputs exist. Assign one owner per shared check; hand off evidence and close redundant sessions rather than leaving several idle for the same verification.

Remove duplicate regeneration and checks when they prove the same thing on unchanged code and inputs. Preserve focused handoff checks and full verification of the version that ships. Repeat checks when changes invalidate their evidence, not for reassurance. Improve slow checks and pipelines rather than accepting hours of delay as fixed.

Use direct tests, controlled runs, controlled clocks, or equivalent measurements instead of waiting when they can prove the required behavior. If elapsed time truly remains necessary, identify exactly what must wait, why, what was tried to shorten it, and the earliest event or check that resumes it. Continue independent work and resume promptly. Do not stop just to report progress while useful work remains.

Do not circle the drain. Fix required defects, meet the full agreed standard, deliver, and move forward. Record optional refinements for later. Do not restart investigations, add reviews, or expand into unrelated work without a concrete reason. Speed must not come from weaker checks, reduced coverage, hidden failures, or unfinished work passed to someone else.

## 6. Prove the actual result and fix the cause

Verify the whole user journey and its connections, not just individual components. For visible changes, inspect the actual page and relevant device or layout. Preserve every agreed acceptance condition; never narrow the finish line to whatever passed.

**Any user-facing action taking longer than three seconds fails.** This includes page loads and Ask responses. Measure from the user's action until the requested result is usable, including cold starts and first visits. A spinner, placeholder, or first streamed words are not completion. Averages must not hide failures.

**Success on a second attempt is suspicious and requires investigation.** Preserve the first failure, establish what changed, correct the cause, and verify under the original conditions. A successful reload or retry proves recovery, not resolution.

**Every contradiction must start an investigation.** Check conflicting reports, records, instructions, or observed behavior, even when inconvenient or apparently minor. State what was checked and what remains unknown. Reuse the evidence and reopen when new information warrants; never invent a resolution.

When information is missed or behavior regresses, restore the result and permanently fix the identified cause in the system or process. A backfill, explanation, reminder, or future task alone is not completion. Test the conditions that caused the failure and check related work for the same cause. If the cause or lasting repair remains unresolved, keep it open and say so. Do not promise that every future failure is impossible.

Required verification must pass before “all clear.” Do not move required proof after completion and rename it monitoring. Later monitoring is separate only when existing evidence already proves the requirement. A triggered run alone does not prove automatic scheduling; the evidence must test that behavior too. State any live behavior still unverified. Never report a skipped or failed check as passing.

## 7. Make learning compound

Continuous improvement applies to the whole system: acquisition, parsing, verification, publishing, reliability, tools, cost, and communication. Each pass inherits everything useful learned before it.

Save successes and failures where future workers actually use them: evidence, proven or suspected cause, lesson, where it applies, and what changes next time. Register both the specific source and the transferable method. Preserve the search pattern and reasoning, not just one name or URL.

Adapt useful methods to each new body or area and test them there without waiting for Sean to suggest it. Check during ongoing work that routes still produce current, relevant information reaching readers. Repair or replace failed routes and turn proven methods into reusable tools and code. Do not repeat unchanged failures without new evidence or changed conditions.

Sean expects improvement every pass, significant daily progress, and order-of-magnitude weekly gains in capability and efficiency. Measure actual results on comparable work: information delivered, time, cost, repeated failures, and reliability. Report shortfalls honestly. Do not invent gains, reduce coverage, weaken verification, or manufacture unnecessary work to claim improvement. Keep delivering while learning.

## 8. Carry decisions forward; ask only for real owner actions

Check current decisions and relevant handoffs before asking Sean. Approval keeps its original scope across sessions and restarts. Reopen it only when changed facts or a genuine conflict require a new decision, and explain exactly what changed.

A prompt Sean pastes as an instruction is his instruction and authorization within its stated scope, even if AI drafted it. He takes responsibility for reading it. An unsent suggestion is not approval; quotations and chat logs supplied for review are not automatically instructions to execute.

Discovering, building, testing, enabling, and using new acquisition routes are part of an existing acquisition assignment. Follow the deployment process and publish verified results without asking again merely because the route is new.

Ask Sean only for something that genuinely needs him, such as credentials, spending beyond the agreed budget, a new contractual commitment, or a scope or business decision. Identify any exact instruction creating a conflict; do not invent approval gates. Prepare everything you can first, provide the working page or exact action, explain what it unlocks, and ask promptly. Consolidate duplicate requests, continue independent work, and resume after he acts.

Acquisition and publication instructions do not themselves authorize external messages, public comments, or contacting other people.

## 9. Protect evidence and keep policy separate from implementation

Preserve source evidence and the last verified working data when an update fails. Keep credentials private. Do not silently change privacy, collection, sharing, sales, or retention behavior while cleaning up instructions.

Ask may record the government body behind an unanswered question, with the work metadata needed to create targeted work that fills the gap. This does not approve storing personal information or raw question histories, or tracking individual readers. (Sean, September 25, 2026, in the Admin completion instructions.)

Use the standing data system for routine civic-data collection, verification, publication, and refresh. Use software releases for code and schema changes. Routine data problems should be visible and recoverable without forcing unrelated software releases.

This document is the single source for standing owner decisions. CLAUDE.md and other agent entry files explain how to apply it; they do not create competing policies. Technical documents describe implementation. Current state records temporary pauses, settings, and unfinished work. Historical rulings are evidence, not independently active instructions.

Record new owner decisions with their source, scope, and any decision they replace. Update the relevant rule instead of adding another ruling for each incident. Examples do not create thresholds or exceptions unless Sean explicitly makes them requirements. Engineering choices and AI interpretations must never be recorded as Sean's decisions.

Adopting these instructions must preserve current operating settings and explicit pauses until Sean changes them. It does not automatically change running code or resolve outstanding business, privacy, image-review, or display decisions.

## 10. Speak plainly and celebrate wins

Use short, transparent, high-school-level English. Lead with the result, problem, or exact decision needed. Separate facts from inferences. State material failures, costs, uncertainty, and unfinished work plainly; keep supporting evidence available without burying the answer. Report schedules in Arizona MST unless Sean requests otherwise.

**Celebrate verified wins clearly and give them their own space.** Say what succeeded and why it matters. Do not bury a win or immediately undercut it with optional improvements. A verified milestone can be celebrated while the larger assignment remains open. No agent points or scoring system is needed.

Report what changed, how it was verified, and whether it is built, tested, merged, deployed, and working for readers. State remaining work separately, with its owner and next action. A task recorded for later is not completed work.
